# REST API: Saved queries

These routes of the platform API come from its [OpenAPI document](../openapi.json); [The REST API as a contract](../rest-api.md) says what Lakana promises about them.

## `GET /api/v1/environments/{env}/saved-queries`

List the saved queries of an environment you see

You see your own saved queries (also if you may no longer query the environment), the shared ones (`visibility` `everyone`) if you hold `SUBMIT_QUERY` on it, and, as an instance administrator with a personal token or a session, every one. The items have no `sql` key: read a saved query (`GET .../saved-queries/{saved_query_id}`) for its SQL. A page that shows someone else's private query is recorded in the audit log (`ACTIVITY_VIEWED`); if that fails the answer is 503 and lists nothing. Each item's `actions` says what you may do with it. The order is the name in any letter case, then the id, unless `sort` and `order` ask for another; every order shows the same saved queries. Answers 403 if you may not query the environment, own no saved query there and are not an administrator, 404 if it does not exist, and 403 for a task's token. Send `next_cursor` back as `cursor` with the same sort for the next page.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `env` | path | yes | text | Environment name. |
| `limit` | query | no | whole number | Most items returned (1 to 200). |
| `cursor` | query | no | text or null | The `next_cursor` of the previous page. |
| `sort` | query | no | text or null | What the list is sorted by: `name` (the default, in any letter case), `updated` or `created`. |
| `order` | query | no | text or null | `asc` or `desc`; by default `asc` for `name`, `desc` for `updated` and `created` (the latest first). |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `SavedQueryPageOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `503` | The server cannot do this right now; ask again after the time in `Retry-After`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `SavedQueryPageOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | list of `SavedQueryOut` | yes |  |
| `next_cursor` | text or null | yes |  |

## `POST /api/v1/environments/{env}/saved-queries`

Save SQL under a name in an environment

Needs `SUBMIT_QUERY` on the environment. You become the owner. A saved query is only text: running it is a query you submit with your own rights, never with the owner's. The name is stripped and must be one line of 1 to 200 visible characters, unique among your saved queries in the environment; the SQL must not be empty and at most `LAKANA_QUERY_LIMITS__MAX_STATEMENT_CHARS` long. Answers 403 without the right and for a task's token, 404 if the environment does not exist, 409 for a name you already use there (the message names that saved query's id) and 422 for a refused field.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `env` | path | yes | text | Environment name. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Request body (application/json, required): `SavedQueryIn`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | text | yes |  |
| `sql` | text | yes |  |
| `visibility` | one of `private`, `everyone` | no |  |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `201` | Successful Response | `SavedQueryOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `409` | The request conflicts with the current state; the message says what to change. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `SavedQueryOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | text | yes |  |
| `environment` | text | yes |  |
| `name` | text | yes |  |
| `sql` | text or null | no |  |
| `visibility` | one of `private`, `everyone` | yes |  |
| `owner` | text or null | yes |  |
| `former_owner` | true or false | yes |  |
| `actions` | list of one of `update`, `delete` | yes |  |
| `created_at` | text (date-time) | yes |  |
| `updated_at` | text (date-time) | yes |  |

## `GET /api/v1/environments/{env}/saved-queries/{saved_query_id}`

Read one saved query

You read your own, a shared one if you hold `SUBMIT_QUERY` on its environment, and, as an instance administrator with a personal token or a session, any. An administrator reads the `sql` of a private query that is someone else's only with `READ_QUERY_TEXT`; without it the answer has no `sql` key. Reading someone else's private query is recorded in the audit log (`ACTIVITY_VIEWED`); if that fails the answer is 503 and shows nothing. Answers 404 for a saved query that does not exist and for one you may not see, in the same words, and 403 for a task's token.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `env` | path | yes | text | Environment name. |
| `saved_query_id` | path | yes | text (uuid) | The saved query's id. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `SavedQueryOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `503` | The server cannot do this right now; ask again after the time in `Retry-After`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `SavedQueryOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |

## `PUT /api/v1/environments/{env}/saved-queries/{saved_query_id}`

Replace a saved query's name, SQL and visibility

A whole replacement: send every field, `visibility` included. Only the owner may change a saved query, and only while they hold `SUBMIT_QUERY` on its environment; an administrator who is not the owner may only delete it, and nobody may change one whose owner is gone. The environment never changes: saving in another one is a new `POST`. Answers 403 for anyone but the owner (with a pointer to saving a copy), without the right and for a task's token, 404 for a saved query that does not exist or that you may not see, 409 for a name you already use for another saved query there, and 422 for a refused field or a missing one.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `env` | path | yes | text | Environment name. |
| `saved_query_id` | path | yes | text (uuid) | The saved query's id. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Request body (application/json, required): `SavedQueryUpdateIn`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | text | yes |  |
| `sql` | text | yes |  |
| `visibility` | one of `private`, `everyone` | yes |  |

## `DELETE /api/v1/environments/{env}/saved-queries/{saved_query_id}`

Delete a saved query

The owner deletes their own, with or without `SUBMIT_QUERY` today; an instance administrator (personal token or session) deletes any, which is how a saved query of a deleted owner goes. Answers 403 for anyone else who sees it and for a task's token, and 404 for a saved query that does not exist or that you may not see.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `env` | path | yes | text | Environment name. |
| `saved_query_id` | path | yes | text (uuid) | The saved query's id. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `204` | Successful Response | none |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

## `GET /api/v1/saved-queries`

List the saved queries of every environment you see

Without `environment`, those of every live environment, one cursor across all of them: your own, the shared ones of the environments where you hold `SUBMIT_QUERY`, and, as an instance administrator with a personal token or a session, every one. An environment where you see nothing contributes nothing, so this is never a 403 or a 404, except for a task's token. The items have no `sql` key: read a saved query in its environment for its SQL. A page that shows someone else's private query is recorded in the audit log (`ACTIVITY_VIEWED`, one event per environment shown); if that fails the answer is 503 and lists nothing. With `environment` it is the list of that environment (`GET /api/v1/environments/{env}/saved-queries`), with its 403 and 404. Each item names its `environment`. The order is the name in any letter case, then the environment, then the id, unless `sort` and `order` ask for another. Send `next_cursor` back as `cursor` with the same sort for the next page; a cursor of the list of one environment or of another order is refused with 422 here.

Parameters:

| Name | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | query | no | text or null | Only this environment. |
| `limit` | query | no | whole number | Most items returned (1 to 200). |
| `cursor` | query | no | text or null | The `next_cursor` of the previous page. |
| `sort` | query | no | text or null | What the list is sorted by, with the fields of the list of one environment. |
| `order` | query | no | text or null | `asc` or `desc`, each field's way by default, as on the list of one environment. |
| `authorization` | header | no | text or null | The credential: `Bearer <token>` with a personal access token, task token or CI token. Without it, the web interface's session cookie counts instead. |

Answers:

| Status | Meaning | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | Successful Response | `SavedQueryPageOut` |
| `401` | Not signed in: the token or browser session is missing, wrong, expired or revoked; an ended session says why in `reason`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `403` | Signed in, but not allowed to do this; the message says why and what to do next. | `ErrorOut` |
| `404` | What the request names does not exist, or the caller may not know that it does. | `ErrorOut` |
| `503` | The server cannot do this right now; ask again after the time in `Retry-After`. | `ErrorOut` |
| `422` | Validation Error | `HTTPValidationError` |

Answer fields: `SavedQueryPageOut`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | list of `SavedQueryOut` | yes |  |
| `next_cursor` | text or null | yes |  |
